# Compliance cost of each requirement on the register

*Generated by `alicia/scripts/compliance_costs.py` from `regulation-register/compliance-cost-assumptions.json`, the requirements and the ABS business counts (June 2025). Do not edit by hand. DECISIONS E-700. Draft: compiled by AI-assisted desk research; not yet checked by a person.*

## The figure

Each requirement's **compliance cost** is the staff time it takes the businesses it binds, a year, valued as the Office of Impact Analysis (OIA) values it in its *Regulatory Burden Measurement Framework* (July 2026):

> cost a year = $91.54 an hour × (hours to start × new businesses a year + hours each year × businesses operating)

- **$91.54 an hour** is the OIA's default rate for work time: $52.31 × 1.75 for on-costs and overheads (framework, p. 12). It is read from the burden calculator in `regulatory-burden-tool/`.
- **Hours** are set for each kind of requirement (table below). Every one is **assumed**: no regulator or OIA publication gives standard hours for these tasks. The exceptions are the costings taken from a source, listed below. The 31 costed licences use the licence costs' hours (`docs/licence_costs.md`, E-175), with renewal hours spread over the years between renewals.
- **Businesses** are from the ABS *Counts of Australian Businesses* by industry class, state and employment size, for the classes and states each requirement reaches. A state's rule counts that state's businesses; a Commonwealth rule counts every state's. Its size test picks the size bands, as for the impact classes (E-178): a rule from the first employee counts employing businesses only. **New businesses** are the ABS entries over the year in the same bands.
- **Low and high** values use the low and high hours. The rate and the counts are the same in each.
- Figures are shown to 2 significant figures, because the hours are assumed.

In a steady state every entrant pays the start-up hours once, so this is the framework's yearly average over 10 years for a steady flow of entrants, in constant prices with no discounting (framework, pp. 6–7).

## Upper bounds, and rules not counted

- A rule that binds only **some** of the businesses counted is an **upper bound**, shown as "up to" and kept out of the headline totals. That is a rule above a size threshold the ABS bands can't pin down (a turnover of $100 million, say), one limited to some legal forms, or one that binds only businesses doing an activity ("if it sells alcohol").
- Where that upper bound covers **a quarter or more** of the businesses in the rule's jurisdiction, it says nothing useful about the businesses actually bound, so the rule is **not counted**, and says why.
- A **council's** rule is not costed: business counts by council are not in the panel.
- Requirements of kind **other** are not costed: the obligation varies too much to assume hours.

## What is left out

- **The cost of meeting a standard**: equipment, building work, training, insurance premiums. The OIA calls these substantive compliance costs. They vary too much to assume from public data, so for standards the figure covers only the time to learn the standard and check against it. This is the largest gap.
- **Delay costs**: income lost while waiting for an approval.
- **Fees and taxes** paid to government. The framework leaves them out (p. 4). Where fees are known (the licences), they are shown beside the figure, never in it.
- **Effects on competition and prices**, which the framework also leaves out.
- **Businesses that would do it anyway.** The framework allows these to be netted off; none are here, so figures lean high.
- **Businesses not registered for GST**, which the ABS counts leave out, so very small operators are missed.

| Kind | Requirements | Costed | Task costed | Hours to start | Hours each year | Basis |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Register | 136 | 127 | Register, then keep the details up to date | 1 (0.5 to 3) | 0.5 (0.25 to 1) | Assumed: most registrations are a short online form; updating details is occasional. |
| Hold a licence, permit or accreditation | 943 | 418 | Apply for the licence, then renew it | 4 (2 to 8) | 1 (0.5 to 2) | Assumed, as for the licence costs (E-175): an application means gathering identity, qualification and insurance documents and completing the form; a renewal, taken as yearly, is mostly an online payment. |
| Get an approval for premises, a project or a product | 68 | 46 | Prepare and lodge an application for approval | 0 (0 to 0) | 10 (4 to 40) | Assumed: an approval is sought for each project, premises or product, so it is counted as one application a year for each business bound. Plans, reports and fees paid to consultants are not counted. |
| Notify a regulator | 22 | 9 | Notify the regulator | 0 (0 to 0) | 0.5 (0.25 to 2) | Assumed: one notice a year, mostly a short form. |
| Pay a tax, levy or fee | 90 | 69 | Work out and pay the tax, levy or fee (the time, not the amount) | 0 (0 to 0) | 4 (1 to 12) | Assumed: from one yearly payment to a monthly or quarterly return. The amount paid is a transfer to government and is left out (Regulatory Burden Measurement Framework, p. 4). |
| Hold insurance | 16 | 16 | Arrange and renew the insurance (the time, not the premium) | 0 (0 to 0) | 2 (1 to 4) | Assumed: a yearly renewal. The premium is a substantive cost and is not counted. |
| Report or lodge | 36 | 23 | Prepare and lodge a report or return | 0 (0 to 0) | 8 (2 to 40) | Assumed: one report or return a year. Reports the law requires more often, or audited reports, cost more. |
| Keep records | 4 | 3 | Keep the records the law requires | 0 (0 to 0) | 12 (5 to 26) | Assumed: about an hour a month (central), from 5 hours to half an hour a week. |
| Meet a standard or code | 304 | 266 | Learn the standard and check the business meets it (paperwork and checking only) | 0 (0 to 0) | 8 (2 to 20) | Assumed: keeping up with the standard and checking against it. The cost of meeting it (equipment, building work, training) is not counted. |
| Other | 48 | 0 | Not costed: the obligation varies too much to assume hours | – | – | No default: hours are assumed only where the obligation's kind says what the business does. |

## Costings taken from a source

These requirements take their figures from a source in place of the hours for their kind (E-701). A source may give dollars, not hours: the dollars are then turned into hours at the work rate, so that the working reads the same way. A regulator's list of the entities bound, where there is one, replaces the ABS counts, and the figure is then counted exactly.

### `cth-financial-accountability-regime`: Meet the Financial Accountability Regime obligations

Sourced, from the impact statement for the Banking Executive Accountability Regime (BEAR), which the Financial Accountability Regime (FAR) replaced: Treasury estimated BEAR would cost $11.5 million a year for 149 authorised deposit-taking institutions (4 large, 20 medium, 125 small), upfront costs included, and the Office of Best Practice Regulation agreed the estimate. That is $77,181 an institution a year, taken here as 843 hours at today's work rate. It is in 2017 prices and not indexed. FAR also binds insurers and superannuation trustees, each assumed to cost the same as an average institution under BEAR. The low and high values (half and double) are assumed. No impact analysis costed FAR itself: its explanatory memorandum relies on the Royal Commission's final report, certified in place of one.

- **Hours:** $11,500,000 a year ÷ 149 entities = $77,181 an entity (2017 prices) ÷ $91.54 an hour = 843.1 hours a year (421.6 to 1686.3).
- **Entities bound:** 329 accountable entities APRA regulates, 31 March 2026 (Authorised deposit-taking institutions 128; General insurers 88; Life insurers and friendly societies 32; Private health insurers 28; RSE licensees 53), from Australian Prudential Regulation Authority, [APRA Corporate Plan 2026-27: accessible infographics](https://www.apra.gov.au/apra-corporate-plan-2026-27-accessible-infographics). Non-operating holding companies are also accountable entities but are not counted; APRA's page gives no count of them. ADIs are split across the 4 deposit-taking classes in proportion to the ABS counts.
- **Result:** 843.1 hours × $91.54 × 329 businesses = $25 million ($13 million to $51 million).
- Source: Department of the Treasury (published by the Office of Impact Analysis), [Banking Executive Accountability Regime: Regulation Impact Statement](https://oia.pmc.gov.au/published-impact-analyses-and-reports/banking-executive-accountability-regime), Section 4, Table 2 (regulatory burden estimate) and Appendix B (general assumptions).
- Source: Parliament of Australia (Federal Register of Legislation), [Financial Accountability Regime Bill 2023: Explanatory Memorandum](https://www.legislation.gov.au/bills/C2023B00023EM_1.pdf), General outline, Impact Analysis.

## Totals

Of 1,667 requirements, 977 are costed: 382 exactly and 595 as upper bounds. 182 are not counted because their upper bound covers a quarter or more of their jurisdiction's businesses, and 508 are councils' rules or of kind other.

| | Low | Central | High |
|---|---|---|---|
| Commonwealth requirements, counted exactly | $3 billion | $11 billion | $35 billion |
| State and territory requirements, counted exactly | $770 million | $2.8 billion | $6.9 billion |
| **All requirements counted exactly** | $3.8 billion | **$14 billion** | $42 billion |
| Upper bounds, apart (up to) | $710 million | $2.4 billion | $7.5 billion |

The total is a sum of assumed paperwork time, not an estimate of the burden of regulation. It leaves out substantive compliance costs, the rules not counted, and every law not yet on the register (Victoria has only 32 requirements so far). State totals are not compared, because each state's law is recorded to a different extent.

## Known coding gaps that move a figure

- `cth-payment-times-reporting` binds only large businesses ("reporting entities"), but its triggers carry no revenue threshold, so it is counted at every business. Adding its threshold, with a quote, would make it an upper bound.
- A turnover or revenue threshold above GST's $75,000 can't be counted from employment size bands. The ABS publishes counts by turnover band too; adding them would tighten these upper bounds.

## Files

- `data/processed/legislation/compliance_costs.csv`: one row per requirement, with every input and result.
- `data/processed/legislation/compliance_costs_by_class.csv`: the cost in each ANZSIC class, Commonwealth and state rules apart, and per business in the class.
